draft.title: Victoria Legal Aid
card: Victoria Legal Aid (VLA) is a statutory body set up by the Victorian Parliament. It gives legal help to people in Victoria who might not be able to pay for it.
VLA gives free legal information and advice to anyone who asks, including accused people and victims of crime.
Lawyers are provided only to those who qualify. VLA looks at a person's income and assets, and at the type of case, before it funds a lawyer.
VLA also supports victims of crime, for example by giving them information and advice about the criminal justice process.
draft.remember: VLA gives free advice to all, but a funded lawyer depends on qualifying.

a.q: Tom is charged with theft and has never been to court. He phones VLA for help. What can VLA give him whether or not he qualifies for a lawyer?
opts: Free legal information and advice
A VLA lawyer to appear for him in court
A guarantee that the charge will be dropped
Payment of any fine a court gives him
a.why: VLA gives free information and advice to anyone who asks. A funded lawyer depends on qualifying, so it is not given to everyone. VLA does not decide outcomes or pay fines.
a.clue: Think about what VLA gives to everyone, not only those who qualify.

b.q: Priya is accused of a serious offence. She earns a high income and owns several properties. Which statement best describes her position with VLA?
opts: She may be refused a VLA lawyer but can still get advice
She must get a VLA lawyer because the offence is serious
She cannot get any help from VLA, including information
She gets a VLA lawyer because every accused person does
b.why: VLA considers a person's income and assets, and the type of case, before funding a lawyer. So Priya may not qualify for one. Free information and advice is still open to her, so VLA does not refuse her all help.
b.clue: Funding a lawyer depends on a means test, but advice does not.

b.best: She may be refused a VLA lawyer but can still get advice

problems.detail: The right option is the only hedged one ('may'). The three distractors all use absolutes ('must', 'every', 'cannot any'), so a student could pick the answer by spotting the qualifier without knowing the means test.

check.summary: The facts about VLA's free information and advice and its means-tested lawyers are correct, and both intended answers are right. In question b, the right option is the only one with a qualifier, while every distractor uses an absolute, which gives the answer away.
